definition: A bond in which two atoms share a pair of electrons; both positive nuclei attract the shared pair, and that electrostatic attraction holds the atoms together.
The tendency of atoms to lose, gain or share electrons until they have eight electrons in their valence shell (two for hydrogen); some molecules, such as $\ce{BeCl2}$, break it.
A diagram of a molecule or ion that shows every valence electron, as bonding pairs between atoms and lone pairs on atoms, drawn as dots, crosses or lines.
A pair of valence electrons that belongs to one atom only and is not shared in a bond; for example, the oxygen atom in water has two.
The distance between the nuclei of two atoms joined by a covalent bond; between the same two elements, a triple bond is shorter than a double bond, which is shorter than a single bond.
A covalent bond in which one atom supplies both electrons of the shared pair, as when the lone pair on nitrogen in ammonia bonds to $\ce{H^+}$; also called a dative or coordinate bond.
